records.title: Accept PROXY protocol v1 on webrtc-proxy-protocol-relays (or document that only v2 is supported)
records.author: paper0319
records.evidence: WAVE-9 TRIAGE: feature request for PROXY protocol v1 on UDP relays; NetherNet relays go through NetherNetServer.java:423,731 into cloudburst IceProxyProtocol (v2), and v1 is not officially supported for UDP. Documentation note only.
records.body:
### What feature do you want to see added?

Follow-up to #6835 / #6843. Some DDoS-protection providers only emit PROXY protocol v1 (text) on UDP. Mine (Broccoli Network "DDoS Shield") sends a v1 header on the first datagram of each UDP flow, directly followed by the STUN binding request:

PROXY TCP4 <client-ip> <dedicated-ip> <client-port> 19132\r\n + STUN binding request

The panel only has a Proxy Protocol on/off toggle, and the provider confirmed it does not fully support v2.

records.title: Skin plugin message dropped during join when subscribersCount == 1
records.author: SendableMetatype
records.evidence: MASS-AUDIT: FloodgateSkinUploader.java:137-142 sends skin to server manually when subscribersCount==1 or allowSubscribers off.
records.body:
### Describe the bug

When `subscribersCount == 1` (Floodgate's websocket is not connected), `FloodgateSkinUploader` sends skin data to the backend via `PluginMessageUtils.sendMessage()` on the `floodgate:skin` channel. This message is sent during the player join process and arrives at Velocity while `getConnectedServer()` is still null, causing Velocity to silently drop it. The skin never reaches the backend and the player appears as Steve/Alex to Java players.

records.title: Bedrock Spectator Mode not working as intended.
records.author: NQNAMER
records.evidence: WAVE-3-AUDIT: https://github.com/GeyserMC/Geyser/issues/6248 — entity spectating is already implemented in the integrated source on integration/final-release @ 96a2e130095d4337c78cfc4ff69b5479446c6ad1: core/src/main/java/org/geysermc/geyser/entity/EntitySpectateHelper.java:46,59-84,112-120 (start/stop/cycle/tick, first/third-person modes) and core/src/main/java/org/geysermc/geyser/translator/protocol/java/entity/JavaSetCameraTranslator.java:39-45 (ClientboundSetCameraPacket -> start/stop), with tick wiring at core/src/main/java/org/geysermc/geyser/session/GeyserSession.java:1494. Upstream maintainer confirmed the behaviour in 26.2 builds; showing the player self-model while spectating was intentionally declined. No new commit SHA is claimed: the implementation is already present in the integrated source. Reference: https://github.com/GeyserMC/Geyser/issues/6903.
records.body:
### Describe the bug

In newer versions of Minecraft Bedrock Edition, spectator mode has been implemented natively and works similarly to how it does in Minecraft: Java Edition. However, there are still some limitations, such as the inability to spectate entities.

On Java servers using GeyserMC, this functionality was implemented earlier through a workaround. While this allowed Bedrock players to use spectator-related features before Bedrock supported them natively, the current implementation still has some inconsistencies and bugs.

___________________________________________________________

records.evidence: MASS-AUDIT: Maintainer Redned235: "Very little we can do here given this behavior is a result of ViaVersion... outside of our control." (issue #3922).
records.body:
### Describe the bug

Found a problem, maybe is a bug?
For 1.12.2 spigot with viaversion and new world.
Viaverson will send extra `ClientboundSectionBlocksUpdatePacket` to client when the chunk load.
But the `ClientboundSectionBlocksUpdatePacket.entries`'s size is 4096.
So per SubChunk will send at least about 9000 times `UpdateBlockPacket` to Bedrock client.
This will make client lag when load chunk.

### To Reproduce

1. run a new spigot 1.12.2 server with viaversion.
2. join with geyser.
3. /gamemode creative
4. fly forward.
5. Now the client will lag.

### What feature do you want to see added?

records.evidence: MASS-AUDIT: Custom fog and camera shake in baseline: core/src/main/java/org/geysermc/geyser/session/GeyserSession.java:2742 shakeCamera, :2747 stopCameraShake, :2752 sendFog.
records.body:
### What feature do you want to see added?

Bedrock has the ability to display custom fog and enable a camera-shaking effect to the player's view via commands. However, since Java normally has no support for either of those, this severely limits what kind of immersion can be achieved on the server side. If this is possible, it would be a big change for servers that want to enhance the experience significantly for Bedrock players, while keeping in mind Java players won't see any of those effects without relying on alternatives like FOV-based shake via slowness effect and vision-altering mob eff

records.title: Bedrock coordinate issue workaround
records.author: ghost
records.evidence: CLOSED_NOT_VERIFIED: closed != fixed, audit required | AUDIT-15E: upstream closed with state_reason=not_planned; closed as not planned without a verifiable fix. No fixing commit in master.
records.body:
### What feature do you want to see added?

Bedrock struggles with coordinates over 64000, and they show no plans to fix the bug, my suggestion is to segment a world into 64000x64000 segments, so for example if the player is at the coordinates 64023 100 1034, all packets sent to them have their location changed to 23 100 1034 to fix precision loss. When a player crosses the 64000 segment border the world can be reloaded to fix any weird behavior.

### Are there any alternatives?

There are no alternative for non world bordered survival servers

There is some encryption-related bug where players are only able to play for a short time before communication essentially ceases and no actions go through to Geyser if the server is running a 10th or 11th generation Intel processor. records.evidence: MASS-AUDIT: Merged PR #2688 'Allow single-device Microsoft authentication' addresses #2496 2FA login; baseline GeyserImpl.java:871 caches MsaAuthenticationService/auth chains.
records.body:
### What feature do you want to see added?

When logging in with Microsoft account using mail and password (while having 2FA enabled on the account), it should continue the login dialog and wait until the user approves the login request in Microsoft authenticator, instead of disconnecting the user for invalid credentials. 

### Are there any alternatives?

You could use the web browser login, but when you are on the go where you don't have another device, you simply can't login.

records.title: Feature request: the ability to store login tokens
records.author: jackson-57
records.evidence: MASS-AUDIT: Requested stored login tokens; baseline GeyserImpl.java:865-890 saves auth chains via savedUserLogins()/savedAuthChains to disk.
records.body:
**What feature do you want?**
I think that there should be a way to store login tokens, instead of saving your Minecraft/Microsoft account's credentials in a plaintext config file. A toggle could be added to the online mode login prompt, which lets the user choose if they'd like to stay logged in.

**Alternatives?**
This would be a much more secure alternative to the userAuths system currently implemented in Geyser. Additionally, since Microsoft accounts support OAuth, it would allow the user to stay logged in without ever handing Geyser their account credentials.

Sending the actual text content works, but defeats the point of lang.

**What feature do you want?**
As discussed in #1386 it would be great if you could add a possibility to set only *some* options in a config file before starting the server for the first time by creating a partial config file like this:
```
bedrock:
  clone-remote-port: true
```
On the first start the plugin would generate the full config including the values of the partial config.

**Alternatives?**
An alternative is getting a predefined config and using that to change some options. The downside is that this could break with updates.

records.title: Players can't connect with Bedrock without opening another connection first
records.author: Doctacosa
records.evidence: CLOSED_NOT_VERIFIED: closed != fixed, audit required | AUDIT-17K: closed as support/config/feature request rather than a code defect; maintainer: "Are you on our Discord? This is definitely not a one-time problem; while our developers have never been able to replicate it we've heard reports of users saying it's a thing."
records.body:
**Describe the bug**
Some Bedrock players using Windows 10 Edition aren't able to connect to the server, or even see it as online in their servers list. The only way to make it work is to initiate a connection to the same IP address through any other means, which can be by using a Java client, open a website on the same server, run nmap, or something similar. Once that's done, they have a working window of about 30 minutes to connect. After that duration has elapsed, the server will appear to be inaccessible once again. Two of the affected players seem to have a 100% reproduction rate so far.

records.title: Delay command autocomplete

records.body:
**What feature do you want?**
On a big server with lots of plugins, entering a slash `/` causes a lag up to 15 seconds due to the huge amount of commands the client recieves. How about delaying that to at least when a letter is added, so e.g. `/e` would give a smaller amount of commands to autocomplete.

Workarounds include copying slash + letter or typing a letter before slash to avoid autocomplete until the command is written.

records.title: Support the PROXY protocol
records.author: bundabrg
records.evidence: MASS-AUDIT: Merged PR #1713 'HAProxy PROXY protocol support for upstream connections' body: 'Closes #677'; also #1688 (downstream)
records.body:
**What feature do you want?**

GeyserMC should support the [PROXY Protocol](https://www.haproxy.com/blog/haproxy/proxy-protocol/) both upstream and downstream.

Features:
  * Allows GeyerMC itself it run behind a proxy (like haproxy) and retain IP forwarding.
  * For downstream servers that support it (Bungeecord does) it allows passing IP forwarding on without needing additional plugins.

records.title: Mirror custom block collision boxes on X for 26.60+
records.author: rtm516
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit cb04ea8afe63e76b7c8219810faa47534bf7f2fc; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
Mirrors custom block collision boxes on the X axis for 26.60+ clients, matching BDS. From 1.26.63, BDS writes `minX = 8 - origin.x - size.x` instead of `8 + origin.x`, the same way selection boxes already behave. Older protocols keep the current encoding.

Tested with Hydraulic, where collision boxes can now use the same mirrored origin as selection boxes, so it no longer needs to treat collision boxes differently.

records.title: Reduce resident memory of block registries after startup
records.author: linsaftw
records.evidence: WAVE-6-AUDIT: block-registry resident-memory reduction after startup; upstream PR #6932 (https://github.com/GeyserMC/Geyser/pull/6932) was closed unmerged upstream, but both of its commits 5a8d8d81bd166c1573d163b165fde73bc2ad3fba and 4f8280665f740fe21ff9d868ada9f3c0a415d695 are ancestors of base HEAD 037163fe9092b1caf7b40cc4269e6e1fcda76b09 (verified with git merge-base --is-ancestor) and the memory reduction is present in the fork, so the fix is already integrated despite the unmerged PR — https://github.com/GeyserMC/Geyser/pull/6932
records.body:
Heap analysis of a Velocity proxy running Geyser showed the block registries as the largest Geyser-owned retention (NbtMap data about 26 MB, plus about 5 MB of fastutil index maps).

Changes:
- Intern whole block NbtMaps across the Bedrock palette versions, since most blocks are identical in every palette.
- Release the NbtMap-keyed `stateDefinitionMap` once the item registries are built. It was only used while populating creative items. `BlockMappings#getDefinition(NbtMap)` falls back to a palette scan.
- Trim `JAVA_BLOCK_STATE_IDENTIFIER_TO_ID` to the keys the sound mappings still look up at

records.body:
This PR introduces a new pack format, along with the code to load it, to Geyser. "Geyser asset packs", with the extension `.geyserpack`, are ZIP archives containing Geyser mappings, locale overrides, and Bedrock resource packs.

Geyser packs are put in Geyser's `packs` folder, just like normal Bedrock resource packs. Each Geyser pack must have a `geyser_manifest.json` file, with the following keys:

```json
{
  "format_version": 1,
  "uuid": "db1202bb-8199-4f16-ad9d-1b6d78f653a9",
  "pack_version": 2
}
```

records.title: Add texture variation and alpha masked tint to material instance API
records.author: rtm516
records.evidence: WAVE-8: textureVariation/alphaMaskedTint added additively to MaterialInstance (default methods, no API version bump), stored in GeyserMaterialInstance, read from material JSON by BlockMappingsReader_v1 and packed into packed_bools by CustomBlockRegistryPopulator. :api:compileJava + :core:compileJava + item translator tests green.
records.body:
Adds `textureVariation` and `alphaMaskedTint` to the `MaterialInstance` API.

Material instance flags are now sent as the `packed_bools` bitset, matching BDS: (thanks Claude for helping me work these out)

| Bit | Flag |
|---|---|
| `0x1` | face dimming |
| `0x2` | isotropic |
| `0x4` | texture variation |
| `0x8` | alpha masked tint |

Isotropic was being sent as its own NBT tag rather than as part of `packed_bools`, so it never did anything. That's fixed now.

The custom block mappings now read `isotropic`, `texture_variation` and `alpha_masked_tint`.

Tested in game with epic, legendary and an animated style.

records.title: Add use-haproxy-protocol-webrtc to read HAProxy headers on NetherNet traffic
records.author: tommasov03
records.evidence: MASS-AUDIT: Feature in baseline: NetherNetServer.java:385-386 sets NETHER_SERVER_PROXY_PROTOCOL from webrtcProxyProtocolRelays; GeyserConfig.java:599.
records.body:
Adds the secondary config option discussed in #6835, so Geyser can read PROXY protocol v2 headers on NetherNet (WebRTC) traffic.

## Why

`use-haproxy-protocol` only reaches built-in signaling's TCP listener. A proxy that relays NetherNet media therefore has no way to pass the player's address on it. records.title: Share the Java server's port with built-in NetherNet signaling
records.author: PanSzelescik
records.evidence: AUDIT-15E: upstream PR closed unmerged (decided against); no fixing commit in master, nothing applicable to the fork.
records.body:
## Description
When the Bedrock port is the same as the Java server's port (e.g. with `clone-remote-port`, which many hosting providers rely on), built-in signaling can't bind its TCP listener, so Geyser falls back to the external signaling service. Players then can't join using the server's own `IP:port`.

records.title: Close Floodgate skin uploader websocket during shutdown
records.author: HP-network
records.evidence: MASS-AUDIT: Identical title 'Close Floodgate skin uploader websocket during shutdown' to tracker record 4518933490 (#6700)
records.body:
Fixes #6695

### What changed

Skip a delayed skin-uploader reconnect once shutdown has started.

### How

The scheduled reconnect checks the uploader's `closed` flag before calling `reconnect()`. This prevents a reconnect task queued before executor shutdown from starting new WebSocket threads after Geyser has finished shutting down.

### Testing

- `git diff --check`
- `./gradlew :core:compileJava --no-daemon --console=plain` (blocked by the repository's existing Blossom `baseSet.properties` validation with the bundled Gradle version)

records.title: Add GeyserConnection#updateForm
records.author: Deichor
records.evidence: AUDIT-15C: PR closed by maintainer as AI generated; no code adopted | Closing comment (Novampr): "If you still wish to continue this PR, please reopen it, otherwise I'm closing it because it's AI generated" | https://github.com/GeyserMC/Geyser/pull/6651
records.body:
A plugin that wants to change a form it has already sent has to send it again,
which closes the open form and opens another. The player sees the menu leave and
come back, and any scroll position goes with it.

`ServerSettingsResponsePacket` is applied to a form the client still has on
screen, so its content is replaced in place. There is no separate update packet.

This adds `GeyserConnection#updateForm(Form)`, which returns `false` when no form
is open. The form being replaced is dropped from the cache, so it is not resent
later or answered twice.

Tested on 1.21.130 with a custom form update

records.title: fix: fallback to overworld clock when ViaVersion strips dimension data
records.author: VitzS7
records.evidence: MASS-AUDIT: Exact same title and near-identical body as tracker PR 4135522977 (#6571). Duplicate submission of the overworld-clock fallback fix.
records.body:
## What
ViaVersion translates 1.21.11 → 1.26.2 and removes the `default_clock` field from dimension data. The existing `COMMON_CLOCKS` map only matches exact `overworld` and `the_end` keys, which fails when ViaVersion changes the dimension namespace. Bedrock players get a frozen sky stuck at daytime.

## Fix
Added a general fallback: if no clock was resolved by either the packet data or the `COMMON_CLOCKS` map, and the dimension is not nether-like, default to the overworld clock. This covers custom Multiverse dimensions and any weird namespaced keys ViaVersion might produce.

## Testing
- 1.21

## What changed

This PR improves support for custom Java blocks on Bedrock clients.

Some custom block systems use vanilla block states for visual display while storing the real block data separately. Because Geyser only sees the visual state, block breaking speed and crack animations can become incorrect or out of sync.

This change adds an API that allows extensions to provide the real custom block state and current breaking progress to Geyser. It also improves crack animation synchronization between Java and Bedrock players and clears old crack animations when a block is replaced.

records.title: Fix beds being invisible on Bedrock when loaded from a chunk
records.author: Morningstar-Garden
records.evidence: MASS-AUDIT: BedBlock.java:34 implements BedrockChunkWantsBlockEntityTag; :44-47 builds Bed tag with color on chunk load
records.body:
Beds are a block on Java but a block entity on Bedrock, so Geyser has to send a
Bedrock bed block entity for them to render. `BedBlock` only did this in
`updateBlock` (i.e. when a bed is placed), so beds arriving via chunk load —
after a relog, or when a chunk re-enters render distance — were sent without a
block entity and rendered invisibly.

Implement `BedrockChunkWantsBlockEntityTag` on `BedBlock` (as `LecternBlock` and
the other Bedrock-only block entities do) so the bed block entity, carrying its
color, is also sent on chunk load.

records.title: Fix Java player skins not rendering on Bedrock when texture signature is absent
records.author: rozfourn
records.body:
### Problem

`PlayerEntity`'s `GameProfile` constructor calls `profile.getTextures(true)`, which requires a valid texture signature. Every other texture call site uses `false`:

- `skin/SkinManager.java` → `profile.getTextures(false)`
- `entity/type/player/AvatarEntity.java` → `profile.getTextures(false)`

When a player's `textures` property has no signature (`signature=null`), `getTextures(true)` throws, the `catch` sets `textures = null`, and that player renders as the default (Steve) skin for Bedrock viewers.

records.title: Include common default clocks for vanilla dimensions, which are not sent by ViaVersion
records.author: eclipseisoffline
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit 0d65b201f26c1ecdf676df26463081119a55d291; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body: This PR adds a map of common default clocks for vanilla dimensions, to be used as fallback when no default clock is sent by the server (or more commonly, ViaVersion). This should resolve some time issues occurring with the latest release of ViaVersion, which started happening because ViaVersion started sending more than one world clock (`overworld` and `the_end`), which caused Geyser's fallback system in `JavaSetTimeTranslator` (which is to check if there is only one clock registered, and if so, always use that) to fail.

Java clients automatically render passengers as rotating with their vehicle, but Bedrock requires the passenger's own rotation packet. records.title: Only enable BedrockSession packet logging in debug mode
records.author: ByteExceptionM
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit 0cc3317807620e9d72351d74261945e52020d206; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
With `setLogging(true)`, every inbound and outbound Bedrock packet triggers `BedrockSession.logInbound`/`logOutbound`. These call `log.trace(...)` with the packet as a parameter, which materializes `packet.toString()` and routes the record through SLF4J.

Normally an SLF4J TRACE call is cheap when the underlying logger filters it out - the record never gets constructed. But this breaks down on BungeeCord.

BungeeCord's `BungeeLogger` sets its root logger to `Level.ALL`. Every SLF4J call made from within BungeeCord's classloader (which includes Geyser when run as a plugin) is routed through

records.body: Most biome sections in a world are uniform (same biome across all 64 cells). Instead of always computing a full 4096-entry BitArray, we now check if all entries are the same first and use a SingletonBitArray in that case. Skips a lot of unnecessary work for the common case.

records.title: Eliminate ByteBuf copy in chunk translator
records.author: ByteExceptionM
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit 7a917438a8e92f012d393c6ecd3e7dff5fcb769a; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body: The chunk translator was copying the ByteBuf into a byte array and then wrapping it again into a new buffer for the packet. That means every chunk that gets sent briefly exists twice in memory. Removed that extra copy by passing the buffer directly to the packet via `retainedSlice()`. This cuts memory usage per chunk in half during translation and reduces GC pressure, especially noticeable when players are loading lots of chunks at once.

Because in Bedrock Edition, right-click will sends a lot of packets to the server short time, and Geyser limits the rate, this can sometimes cause block placement to fail, as shown in the video.

The reason this happens is: when the player is moving while placing blocks, the packets they send include block faces like UP... UP... SIDE....
At that moment, if Geyser processes the last UP interaction, the following SIDE interaction may get canceled by Geyser. When that happens, the block placement fails.

records.author: valaphee
records.body:
Dynamic recipes, recipes which are not registered beforehand through the recipe book, don't show up with NBT, which is a regression to before.

There is also sometimes the issue that recipes are registered incorrectly, or that recipes depend on NBT and there are multiple recipes with the same base item.

ViaVersion might also always add NBT to certain items, which makes the crafting output non stackable.

This PR solves this by always re-registering dynamic recipes and not keeping them.

records.title: Fix: Shelf block entity items rendered in wrong slot for Bedrock clients
records.author: LPettay
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit 2f1cb9b708d8dff0448aea97198d42de191297ca; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
Bedrock determines shelf item position by list index, not by a `Slot` tag. The previous implementation streamed Java's sparse `Items` list (which only contains occupied slots), so items would shift left into the wrong visual position. For example, an item in slot 1 (middle) would appear in slot 0 (left) on Bedrock.

This fix produces a dense 3-element list with empty item entries for unoccupied slots, so each item lands at the correct list index matching its Java `Slot` value.

**Before:** `[{item}]` → Bedrock renders in slot 0 (wrong)
**After:** `[{empty}, {item}, {empty}]` → Bedrock renders

# Using Pattern.compile() vs matches() for Regular Expressions in Java

This PR optimizes the memory usage for reset pattern in Java.

## Why Pattern.compile() is Preferred Over matches()

When working with regular expressions in Java, using `Pattern.compile()` is significantly more efficient than `matches()` for several reasons:

1. **Performance Optimization**: `matches()` recompiles the regex pattern on each call, while `Pattern.compile()` only compiles it once.

# Using Pattern.compile() vs replaceAll() for Regular Expressions in Java

This PR optimizes the memory usage for reset pattern in Java.

## Why Pattern.compile() is Preferred Over replaceAll()

When working with regular expressions in Java, using `Pattern.compile()` is significantly more efficient than `replaceAll()` for several reasons:

1. **Performance Optimization**: `replaceAll()` recompiles the regex pattern on each call, while `Pattern.compile()` only compiles it once.

2. **Memory Efficiency**: Precompiled patterns reduce memory usage and garbage collection overhead.

records.title: Feature: Allow to change the maximum stack size of custom vanilla item mappings
records.author: BUGTeas
records.evidence: MASS-AUDIT: Feature in baseline: CustomItemRegistryPopulator.java:504-510 reads MAX_STACK_SIZE and sets bedrock max_stack_size; API NonVanillaCustomItemData.stackSize().
records.body:
Now Java editon have the `max_stack_size` component to allow user change the maximum stack size of vanilla items butween 1~99. But Bedrock only support it in addon-defined items, so it's imperfect use.

This pull allow to customize the maximum stack size during the Bedrock item registration. to improve the experience as much as possible.

### Example usage of this pull

JSON mappings:
```json
{
  "format_version": "1",
    "items": {
      "minecraft:snowball": [

records.title: Switch config system to Configurate
records.author: Camotoy
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit 765128ce42ecf3c8418c4134c6e4e014579e884a; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
The primary goal of this PR is to facilitate config changes required for the Floodgate merge, while also allowing for automatic config file generation and updates, as well as customizing configs depending on the features available to a platform.

We have also decided to remove usage of the Jackson library within Geyser. While it has its benefits over Gson, ultimately all platforms have Gson access (and our libraries utilize Gson alongside that) and Jackson is a hefty dependency to shade within Geyser.

records.author: eclipseisoffline
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit 2a6025f3fc841f471c92b23fd2ed982eca36ae4f; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
This PR implements proper reading of data driven enchantments from the server. As of right now, Geyser assumes the `supported_items` and `exclusive_set` tags in enchantments are item and enchantment tags respectively - but this isn't always the case. These tags are holder sets, and can therefore be an item/enchantment ID, an item/enchantment tag, or a list of item/enchantment IDs. This PR properly accommodates for this when reading enchantments.

records.author: eclipseisoffline
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit ff1e1dd7e38f617454b1b439d3056361072b795b; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
This PR fixes the tooltip for attribute modifiers.

Before Java 1.20.5, an attribute modifier was stored with the resource location of the attribute it applies to included in the NBT tag, which Geyser used to get the translation for the attribute modifier, which is displayed in the item tooltip. With the item component changes in 1.20.5, this was changed to instead send the network ID of the attribute to the client.

However, Geyser was updated incorrectly and instead was changed to use the name of the modifier (which is arbitrary and doesn't relate to the attribute it modifies in any way)

records.title: Ensure we send commands/chat the same way a Java client would
records.author: onebeastchris
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit 66f30a2cb6f477ec8ff9d9aa34ec015a6cd6891d; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
Fixes https://github.com/GeyserMC/Geyser/issues/4700

So, interestingly enough, a vanilla Java client is quite.. lenient with whitespaces. Specifically:
- More than one whitespace between words will be normalized to one
- leading/tailing whitespaces are always stripped.

This leads to the interesting case where Bedrock sends a chat packet for the input `   /give @s diamond`, where Java would actually make that a command. Fun!

![image](https://github.com/GeyserMC/Geyser/assets/105284508/3bf6b135-8e4a-41a9-8cd9-90f553f9c7df)

records.title: Add system property Geyser.RakSendCookie to allow disabling cookie send
records.author: Kas-tle
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit 2471de100be3f229bfa415ec887e48a29002d2b2; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
Adds the system property Geyser.RakSendCookie to allow disabling of sending RakNet cookies in environments where it is not supported (e.g. running Geyser behind an older bedrock proxy).

This is meant as a temporary mitigation as we would rather bedrock proxies update to support this. Ideally, this should not be set to `false` unless Geyser is running behind a reverse proxy that is also sending a challenge to prevent IP spoofing.

## Summary

This PR adds:

### System Properties

- `Geyser.RakPacketLimit` system property to set RakNet's per-ip per-tick (10ms) post-connection packet limit (Default: `120`)
- `Geyser.RakOfflinePacketLimit` system property to set RakNet's per-ip per-second pre-connection packet limit (Default: `10`)
- `Geyser.RakGlobalPacketLimit` system property to set RakNet's per-tick (10ms) overall packet limit (Default: `100000`)
- `Geyser.RakRateLimitingDisabled` system property to completely disable RakNet's post-connection rate limiter (Default: `false`)

records.title: Fix: Don't mistakingly assume that Geyser-Velocity initialized
records.author: onebeastchris
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit 06663bcafd8ac19f4072b813fe091e5dbbf4d3de; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
Should fix https://github.com/GeyserMC/Geyser/issues/4275

Suspected issue:
- Query initialized, which fired a ListenerBoundEvent, which caused `INITIALIZED` to be set to true 
- After the proxy started accepting connections, a new ListenerBoundEvent was fired with the `ListenerType.MINECRAFT` - which is when geyser's post startup occurs. However, since `INITIALIZED` was set to true due to the query binding, no injector is created... sorry, my mistake.

This fix should now ensure that `INITIALIZED` is only set after we initialized, and not every time the ListenerBoundEvent was fired.

records.title: Fix: Bedrock clients timing out due to present Java resource packs
records.author: onebeastchris
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit 3547fab228aefe556be948d8a4e650870a526cb5; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
Since 1.20.2, there's a ClientboundResourcePackPacket sent during the configuration phase, which the client is expect to respond to with a ServerboundResourcePackPacket. It contains a `ResourcePackStatus` enum - either `SUCCESSFULLY_LOADED`, `DECLINED`, `FAILED_DOWNLOAD`, or `ACCEPTED`. 

If the client does not respond with one of these in 30 seconds - it can do so automatically if server resource packs are accepted - then the player is kicked due to timing out. Hence, we need to decline the packs - which can lead to a kick if those are required - or we don't get in at all.

records.title: Close threads at server shutdown
records.author: petersv5
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit 7d489c7354b4888b02b5a49c651a9f45249ba170; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
To exit normally all non-daemon threads of the java process are supposed to have stopped. There are several cases of EventLoopGroup-created thread pools that are not shut down as a part of the server shutdown.

These threads are spawned on the first Bedrock player login. The identified cases are:
- TcpClientSocket created by GeyserSession
- The listener threads in GeyserServerInitializer
- The player threads in GeyserServerInitializer
- The EXECUTOR_SERVICE in the SkinProvider

This patch depends on the PR
https://github.com/GeyserMC/MCProtocolLib/pull/744 submitted to MCProtocolLib.

records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit 6eca6ade06943680173535aa8fc481a68fe5c1c2; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
Closes #3882

Old behaviour: if the 1.19.80 palette is processed last, then the fallback mapping for the `relic` record overrides the entry in `Registries.RECORDS`, and all versions hear `wait` instead of `relic`. 

The records registry *could* become versioned, but it doesn't seem worth it.

Now, 1.20 hears the relic disc, and 1.19.80 hears nothing.

records.author: Kas-tle
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit cfd7aeb927d0816a0d7943f370334ec6a876f16c; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
Because the API is now in a separate repo, PRs that rely on API changes will fail to build with the current PR build action. This PR updates the action to check if the user initiating the PR has a fork of the API repo with a branch matching the name of their PR. If this is the case, the action will clone the users API repo and cache it to the action runner's local maven repo before building Geyser. As a result, the action can then use the user's changes to the API when building Geyser.

records.title: Fix wrong render distance calculation
records.author: valaphee
records.evidence: AUDIT-16H: upstream fix commit 3fad4c37fc7993dbbc7e5699df1561762bb782a3 verified ancestor of GeyserMC/Geyser master via compare (status behind, ahead_by=0); fix present in fork at core/src/main/java/org/geysermc/geyser/util/DimensionUtils.java:105 (setRadius(32)); maintainer: "com/GeyserMC/Geyser/commit/3fad4c37fc7993dbbc7e5699df1561762bb782a3 which will eventually land in master"
records.body:
Currently the render distance is calculated by fitting a square into a circle, which is not the way how bedrock does interpret the render distance.

Which can be verified by removing the empty chunk sending in the chunk unload packet, because chunks don't get unloaded anymore at the edge, when directly using the square render distance, chunks getting unloaded as expected.

This also fixes the fog. See #3458

Had this fix already running for a month, without problems so far.

Currently, only the artifacts generated by `shadowJar` and `sourcesJar` are published to Maven repositories. This results in the following files being published:

```
[module]-[version].jar
[module]-[version].pom
[module]-[version]-sources.jar
```

However, this causes problems when another project depends on Geyser because the JAR artifact includes all of Geyser's dependencies which may already be present in the target environment. See GeyserMC/Geyser-Fabric#71 for an example of the problems that can happen as a result of this.

This PR makes Gradle publish the entire `java` compone

records.title: Improve bungeecord ping passthrough integration, fixes motd with mult…
records.author: valaphee
records.body:
# Description

This changes the way how the Geyser ping passthrough in BungeeCord works. Currently the ping passthrough tries to mimic the the InitialHandler behavior for pinging, which for example doesn't respect the ping passthrough configuration of the BungeeCord itself, and doesn't work with forced hosts, etc.

To fix this, I'm directly interfacing the InitialHandler, this should have an identical behavior as legacy ping passthrough.

# Testing

Has been tested on Waterfall with ping passthrough forced hosts enabled and normal ping, and in production environment.

records.title: Events can be handled by any class
records.author: ImDaBigBoss
records.evidence: MASS-AUDIT: Any object can register events via EventRegistrar.java:34 (of(Object)); Extension.java:36 extends EventRegistrar; no EventListener remains in API.
records.body:
The `Extension` class extends `EventListener`, and any class can implement it and then register it:
```java
ClassThatImplementsEventListener eventListener = new ClassThatImplementsEventListener();
GeyserApi.api().eventBus().register(eventListener, eventListener);
```

Also:
* Loggers have the same implementation (`AbstractLogger`) so that we make sure they follow each other
* Stopped the `extensions` folder from being created at the server root for non standalone and moved it into the data folder.

Though there's no direct field in the packet that indicates the user finishes editing, I'm only able to use some tricky way to determine when should we send the packet. records.title: Allow single-device Microsoft authentication
records.author: turikhay
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit d0220a9b71f9c210d5a99a0e5e08583cf19de3f9; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
Related to https://github.com/GeyserMC/Geyser/issues/2496

There is a problem with Microsoft authentication while using GeyserConnect on mobile: player **must** use another device in order to complete it. I created this PR to remove this limitation.

The solution is simple: Geyser caches `MsaAuthenticationService` instance for limited amount of time (e.g. 60 seconds) for each user requesting MS authentication. Users are distinguished by their `xuid`.

records.title: Connect Geyser players directly to the server for plugin versions
records.author: Camotoy
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit 002be32bb37a58a6465776f3df9f84a984ce0688; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
This PR introduces the concept of using Netty's LocalChannel - a channel type that performs the same network actions as a normal Minecraft connection, albeit locally in the Java runtime - in order to join the Java server without requiring a TCP connection. This introduces increased performance, always-correct IP addresses, and less configuration required (`remote` `address` and `remote` `port` are 99% irrelevant for plugin versions with this PR).

The code changes may cause plugin conflicts, but through testing any such problem has been solved.

By updating these dependencies, we bring in a couple fixes that should improve network performance:

- Use TCP_NODELAY for the Java connection
- Use Epoll/KQueue if possible for the Java connection
- Only use one event loop for the Java connection
- Fix Netty dependencies so Spigot and BungeeCord can use native network types

Currently, Geyser-Spigot pre-1.12 breaks with these changes. It is unlikely that this will be fixed.

records.body:
Geyser now supports block picking for item frames. It checks to see if the item frame has an item in it - if so, it attempts the same block picking process with the item inside (NBT included). Otherwise, it attempts to pick for an item frame item.

This commit also improves item frames by having the internal map store the entity and not the ID - in many situations, this prevents two maps from having to be searched. Additionally, item frames are no longer despawned if an item is placed on them - rather, it waits until the server tells us to despawn the entity.

records.title: Fix server switching with larger render distances
records.author: Camotoy
records.evidence: AUDIT-16I: NOT_APPLICABLE - PR closed unmerged as stale/obsolete/rejected; no merged fix commit in this repo.
records.body:
The server only started sending its render distance during 1.14. ViaVersion compensates by sending 64 as the render distance, always - but this can choke up Bedrock in various ways. This PR fixes two separate issues related:

- In some instances, the client would be stuck on Building Terrain during server switch. This is solved by fake-decreasing the render distance during server transfer. Zero issues have been found thus far.
- When switching servers, chunks could be dropped. While not pretty, if the client is not spawned, they are teleported to near the chunks so they cannot be unloaded.

records.evidence: AUDIT-16G: fixed upstream by commit a5779a716bfb "Better handling of invalid items in recipe translator", verified as an ancestor of GeyserMC/Geyser master (GitHub compare behind_by=0); fix at connector/src/main/java/org/geysermc/connector/network/translators/java/JavaDeclareRecipesTranslator.java:85. Closing: "I handled this in https://github.com/GeyserMC/Geyser/commit/a5779a716bfb0d5cfd84eebaf41cd999bd56c021 and added you as a co-author. Thanks!" https://github.com/GeyserMC/Geyser/issues/2133
records.body: I don't know if this can *only* occur when the server has block-adding mods, but I think completely failing to let players craft any items at all would qualify as "bad behavior". This PR filters items from the stonecutter recipe list which would otherwise trigger a NullPointerException, so only the invalid item will be uncraftable, not *all* items.

records.body: Previously, we wouldn't send the time if the server was sending the same time with doDaylightCycle on. However, this isn't vanilla behavior (for Bedrock nor Java) and can occasionally cause irregularities. The time is now always sent to Bedrock clients, and a daylightCycle field is added to GeyserSession to keep track of the doDaylightCycle gamerule we need to send to Bedrock. Removing the map we used to store the time may also improve memory usage since this was never cleaned up.

records.title: Implement Bedrock player collision (pushing)
records.author: Camotoy
records.evidence: AUDIT-16F: maintainer ruled duplicate: "Closing in lieu of #5694"; canonical record GeyserMC/Geyser#5694.
records.body:
This isn't perfect! Feel free to play around and critique the code. I'm no expert in collisions, however; I have to thank `pokechu22` for giving me some excellent reference code to work with.

Unlike fishing rod pulling behavior that is calculated serverside on Bedrock and clientside on Java, Bedrock player "pushing" is nonexistent on Bedrock. This code checks to see if a Geyser player should be moved, and if so applies motion to the player which sends movement packets back.

This commit also cleans up the move relative code of villagers so they aren't always checking the chunk cache.

records.title: Move login process around to provide a better user experience
records.author: bundabrg
records.body:
# Overview

Move around how the login process works to provide a better user experience.

We do this by keeping the "Finding Server" screen up and preloading the downstream connection simultaneously. Only once things are finalized do we then show the world and spawn in all the cached entities.

Supercedes #656

# To Test
* [X] Offline Login
* [x] Online Login with Floodgate

records.title: Translate client-computed recipes
records.author: Camotoy
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit c1a70c77545cac5ddc5b82dfc4422759cb7c3277; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
A handful of recipes are complex enough on Java Edition that the client simply calculates them after getting an assurance that they are valid recipes. This PR stores those recipes in a Bedrock-compatible format in mappings, then generates the CraftingData information on startup to send to the Bedrock client when called. This fixes firework rocket and star crafting, and fixes leather armor and shulker box dyeing.

The recipe information for everything except leather armor was taken right from the Bedrock server. The leather armor had to be created separately (see https://github.com/DoctorMacc

records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit 7fcfa7d54d4fc3b0e6d4416047b0394eb48e962a; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
Until 1.16, enchantment tables were impossible to implement properly in Geyser. When a user selects an enchantment in Bedrock, the client creates the book on its end and assumes the server is OK with it. Java requires a button to be pressed to select the enchantment. With 1.16, server authoritative inventories remove that on Bedrock. However, until our inventory rewrite is finished we are still stuck without enchantment table support. This commit serves as an alterative as we wait.

records.title: Implement Inventory Transactions
records.author: bundabrg
records.body:
## Changes:
* Implement a transaction based system for resolving inventory changes. A new transaction is created which has all the actions to resolve it, with each action optionally requiring a confirmation step. For example all Click/Drops should only proceed after receiving an associated confirm packet otherwise out of order updates occur. This is also done asynchronously.

records.title: Implement Block Mapping Overrides
records.author: bundabrg
records.evidence: AUDIT-17J: PR closed unmerged; maintainer flagged block-mapping override as out of scope and the reported case was a Discord discussion — no accepted fix. — https://github.com/GeyserMC/Geyser/issues/497
records.body:
Not sure if this is useful to anyone else but I needed the ability to selectively override block mappings without needing to recompile. In my case it was to convert an end_gateway block to air for my bedrock players which is not something everyone else would want and thus made sense to be a selective override.

This provides the following changes:

* All attempts to load a resource will first look for the path under a "resources" folder relative to the executable and if not found will be retrieved from the internal resource stream. This allows overriding any resource at runtime by creating

records.author: lukeeey
records.evidence: MASS-AUDIT: Operator features in baseline: GeyserSession.java:1584 setGameMode, WorldManager.java:124-135 setDefaultGameMode/setDifficulty, opPermissionLevel and reducedDebugInfo handling.
records.body:
### Introduction
This pull request allows you to change your game mode, the world difficulty, default game mode and game rules from in-game. Additionally, coordinates will now be hidden if the `reducedDebugInfo` game rule (which only exists in java edition) is enabled.

Due to an issue with MCProtocolLib, difficulty changing is currently disabled.

I have shoved a few things in `WorldManager` so i can override it if Geyser is run as a bukkit plugin which probably wasnt the best way to go about it, but im making this PR now for feedback.

records.title: Fix map colors, remove unnecessary array stream
records.author: Gerrygames
records.evidence: MERGED_UPSTREAM: merge commit 74f869beb572a4b6e9bf456b3e04fc6876abb7c2; already present in fork via shared upstream history
records.body:
There were two main issues with the map colors:
The java edition colors were incorrectly interpreted as an signed byte.
The bedrock edition should be encoded as an unsigned int, but were implicitly casted to a long in the NukkitX protocol/network dependency. This is fixed by updating to the newest version of the NukkitX protocol.

Also removed the array stream which wasn't necessary nor made anything any simpler.

records.title: Replace spaces in username with _
records.author: bundabrg
records.body:
Bedrock allows spaces but Java Edition does not (or should not). Bad things happen when a user logs in with a space.

This PR simply replaces spaces with _'s. This has the following consequences:

1. Potentially opens a vulnerability for a user with an _ that another user with a space (or vice versa) could log in and be treated as the same user.  I'm not sure if Microsoft already disallow registering a name with an space replaced by an underscore.

2. It may cause other unintended effects so will need testing. One way to test if you don't have a space in your name (because why would you)
